Effects of estrogen: The corpus luteum produces a moderate amount of estrogen. It supports the lining of the endometrium.
Effects of progesterone: The corpus luteum produces progesterone, which becomes the dominant hormone. Progesterone helps the endometrium to become receptive to implantation. It also produces a negative feedback on the brain, decreasing the production of LH and FSH.
Effects of FSH: The level of FSH decreases because of the negative feedback caused by progesterone. This prevents furter development of ovarian follicles.
Effects of LH: As progesterone becomes the dominant hormone, it triggers a negative feedback that reduces the production of LH.
Energy Levels Text: You may still experience high energy from ovulation, still making it easier for high intensity activities. Muscles may work longer without getting tired, and it the body will burn fat and not glucose. The best exercises to do are low intensity workouts such as cycling and running.
Type of food: During this phase it is best to eat carbs and proteins, as when doing exercise it will make your body rely on glucose less. Foods rich with vitamin B and healthy facts will also help to support hormonal balance, and therefore are recommended.
Example of Food: For further information on the types of food and recipes you can make dependent on the phase you are in,you can find it here.https://elara.care/nutrition/menstrual-cycle-food-chart/#mid-luteal-phase-foods
Concentration Levels: Through the luteal phase, the dynamic complexity of the brain remains high but the activity patterns change. This supports deeper thinking, reflection and social sensitivity. For this time it is best to focus on work that requires close attention to detail, deep thinking, and planning.
Health aspect: The luteal phase normally does not vary in length. If your luteal phase is 10 days or less it is recommended you go talk to a specialist as there is a possibility that you may experience Luteal phase deficiency (LPD). Some possible symptoms include spotting, short cycle, and >10 day luteal phase. This disease may contribute to infertility and lead to miscarriages.
Types of Vitamins: During the luteal phase the best vitamins and supplements to take consist of Vitamin B6, magnesium and zinc. Vitamin B6 will help reduce premenstrual symptoms and support hormonal balance. As well as zinc contributing to help support hormonal balance. The magnesium will help to reduce bloating and regulate mood swings.

What is happening in the Uterus: The uterus is prepared for a possible implantation.
What is happening in each phase: The corpus luteum produces progesterones, it decreases the production of LH and FSH and prepares the uterus to welcome the implantation.
